summary: Indeterminate wait indicators: spinner for in-console waits, fuse for brand moments, pulse for Iris thinking.

pairs.dont: Put a spinner where you already know the layout that is coming.
pairs.do: Use Skeleton when the shape is known; keep the spinner for small regions with nothing to stand in for.
pairs.why: A skeleton promises the layout and stops the page jumping. A spinner only says 'wait'.

pairs.dont: Use Fuse for a table refresh or anywhere inside the console.
pairs.do: Keep Fuse for app boot, the widget's first run and empty states — one on screen, at least 56px.
pairs.why: It is slow, large and carries IR red, which means critical everywhere else in Clarion. It also repaints every frame.

pairs.do: Name the work: "Bringing your fleet online", "Iris is thinking".
pairs.why: The label is the only thing a screen reader hears, and 'Loading' tells the person nothing.

pairs.dont: Leave the label on when visible text beside the loader says the same thing.
pairs.do: Pass label={null} so it is announced once.
pairs.why: Hearing the same sentence twice reads as a bug.

pairs.dont: Show a loader for a wait that usually ends in 300ms.
pairs.do: Rely on the show delay (Pulse waits 400ms by default; set delay for others).
pairs.why: A loader that appears and vanishes reads as a glitch, not as work.

pairs.dont: Put a Loader next to a button while it saves.
pairs.why: The action and its progress belong in the same place.

a11y: A loader with text is role="status" with aria-live="polite" and the text in an sr-only span. A loader without text is aria-hidden, because an unlabelled live region announces an interruption that says nothing.
Every animation stops under prefers-reduced-motion — but substitutes rather than deletes. Travel becomes a fade, because a spinner that simply stops looks broken rather than busy.
The SVG filter that gives Fuse its gooey merge is aria-hidden and its id is generated with useId, so two loaders on one page cannot collide.
